title: Edwards v. North Texas Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint found administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because the matter was never filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 & 43-2). 23 concurring, 0 dissenting, 1 disqualified (TE Fowler, a member of the respondent presbytery, OMSJC 2.10(d)(3)(iii)).
first_summary: The SJC held that Jared Edwards's complaint against North Texas Presbytery was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, because the case had never been filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 & 43-2). The Commission concurred 23-0, with one member disqualified as a member of the respondent presbytery.
summary: The SJC held that Jared Edwards's complaint against North Texas Presbytery was administratively out of order and could not be put in order, because the case had never been filed with the presbytery or adjudicated below (BCO 42-4 & 43-2). No merits were reached. The ruling drew 23 concurrences and no dissent; TE Fowler was disqualified as a member of the presbytery party (OMSJC 2.10(d)(3)(iii)). The decision illustrates the SJC's threshold filing requirement: a complaint that bypassed the lower court cannot proceed.
